value.text: Here is a 3-day itinerary in Rome for two kids with a budget of €300, split evenly between the two of you. Day 1: The Colosseum & Roman Forum (€125) Start early to beat crowds and heat at the Colosseum entrance; buy tickets via the official site to save time. Spend the afternoon exploring the adjacent Roman Forum for a relaxed stroll, then end your day with an evening walk along the Palatine Hill. Day 2: Vatican City & St. Peter's Square (€105) Visit the Vatican Museums and St. Peter's Basilica first thing in the morning; reserve tickets online well in advance as they sell out quickly. Afterward, take a short train ride to St. Peter's Square for lunch. Conclude with an evening stroll through the Piazza Navona to see Michelangelo's fountains. Day 3: Archaeological & Shopping Spots (€105) Begin your third day at the Palatine Hill or Villa Giulia for history buffs, then head to the Tiber Island for a refreshing walk and lunch overlooking the river. Finish the trip with a relaxed evening in Trastevere for dinner and a chance to visit the famous shops and narrow streets that end the historic tour. Total: €315 (Note: This estimate assumes standard single tickets, which is slightly over your budget by €15; you may need to combine some attractions or purchase regional passes to stay within €300).
